## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design a practical, scalable scheduler that handles per-key ordering under dynamic workloads—a common real-world constraint in CI systems.

## Key Concepts
- Per-repo in-order guarantees with dynamic worker pools
- Bounded queues and credit-based backpressure
- Dynamic scaling without violating safety invariants

## Code Example
A dispatcher with per-repo FIFO buffers ensures ordering. Each repository has a dedicated channel; the dispatcher routes tasks to available workers while tracking the next expected build_id per repo to enforce in-order execution. When a task arrives out of order, it is held in a buffer until its predecessor completes. The global queue is bounded with a configurable backpressure policy: either delay (pause ingestion until space frees) or drop (reject new tasks when capacity is reached). Workers can be added or removed at runtime by updating the worker pool; the dispatcher continues routing tasks without interruption.
